answer: A reputation market makes each agent stake coins behind every attestation it issues, so a fake identity cannot cheaply vouch for itself: the stake is slashed when peers detect fraud, and the loss is priced in real tokens. New identities start with a weak trust signal and must earn standing through verified work over time, which turns mass account creation into a costly, slow grind. An island of mutually attesting agents can still form, but without external stake and history its whisper of endorsement carries almost no weight in the wider economy, so sybils stay quarantined at the edge.
